scope: Native interaction scheduling, workspace layout and sidebar/tab presentation; Chromium engine unchanged.
changes: Removed double-sided flip capture, overlays, settings and global event tap; existing two-window groups use ordinary tabs.
Preserved native layout animations and excluded their own geometry notifications from layout/persistence invalidation.
Native mutation revisions replace repeated tree snapshots and permit unchanged layouts, normalization and presentation to be reused.
Shared layout plans, native sidebar/tab data and organized browser rows are cached with identity, state and configuration invalidation.
Input focus precedes deferred coalesced chrome publication; suspended stale model builds cannot publish.
Mouse-release discovery targets clicked/dragged apps; unknown targets retain coalesced rate-limited global recovery.
Already-hidden workspace repair runs outside the input path with visibility, ownership, monitor and cancellation guards.
Unchanged session inputs skip checkpoint scheduling; edits arriving during disk I/O schedule a trailing save.
Removed synchronous stack symbolication on every native tree unbind.
Added browser layout dispatch/reply/timeout signposts and 200-page/soak options to the live switching probe.
benchmark_configuration: Optimized Swift release with -DDEBUG, same machine/workloads; after measurements use --skip-build with compilation stopped.

live_qualification.reason: The running workspace owns the native-management lease; isolated switching fixtures refuse to displace it.

limitations: CPU benchmarks are synthetic, not input-to-present or compositor measurements.
No end-to-end speedup, idle-energy reduction or memory-reduction claim is made.
Full discovery remains for recovery and unclassified events; browser inventory and structural edits conservatively invalidate layout caches.
Existing unrelated working-tree changes were retained. No installed app has been replaced.
